sections.name: Headcrab
sections.card:
Summary: A small, weak parasite with 10 health and a 5-damage bite. It is a real nuisance in numbers, mostly because you stop noticing it while you deal with something bigger.
Weak points: Its underside: a crowbar swing at it while it leaps kills it in one hit, and gravity gun bursts are easy to land on it. It cannot swim, and drowns if it falls into deep water.
Looks like: A round, smooth, tan body on four legs, about two feet long, with a round mouth underneath.
Tips: Keep moving when headcrabs are about. A pistol suits a few of them, the shotgun short to medium range, and the SMG a big group; one hand grenade can clear headcrabs and zombies together.
Tips: If poison headcrabs are mixed in, kill those first. A headcrab cannot hurt you while you are in a vehicle.

sections.name: Fast Headcrab
sections.card:
Summary: A lanky, very quick headcrab with the same 10 health and 5-damage bite as the ordinary kind. It can bite again sooner than the others, which adds up when several come at you.
Looks like: A slim body covered in wart-like bumps, on long, evenly sized legs that end in claws, with no fangs showing outside the mouth.
Tips: It dies to anything that kills an ordinary headcrab, but its speed makes the crowbar and pistol harder to land. Shoot it from a distance; the MP7's fast fire and spread work well on one or a group.
Tips: In dark places one may cling to the ceiling and drop on you, or when a light triggers it, so check overhead. When one gets close, back off or keep it in sight so you can kill it right away.

sections.name: Poison Headcrab
sections.card:
Summary: A slow, dark headcrab with 35 health. Its bite drops you to 1 health at once; your suit's antidote then slowly brings you back up, a little short of where you were.
Looks like: Dark skin and long, bristly legs with red joints crossed by a white band; the biggest of the headcrabs, with a bulky body.
Tips: It is slow and rattles before it jumps, so sidestep; moving backwards can still get you bitten. It tends to hide, but its sounds give it away, so kill it before the other enemies.
Tips: One shotgun blast at close range, one .357 shot at any range, or one crowbar hit kills it; a pistol takes many shots.

sections.name: Zombie
sections.card:
Summary: The ordinary zombie: a person taken over by a headcrab, relentless and tougher than a normal human. It swings objects in its way at you, and some lie still among corpses and rise when you come close.
Weak points: The headcrab on its head: when it dies or comes off, the host dies too. Aim for the head; a double shotgun blast there is a guaranteed kill.
Looks like: A rotting, decayed body whose hands have turned into claws, with a headcrab on its head.
Tips: A zombie ignores fire, electricity and traps that are not in its way. A body in a heap of corpses that still has a headcrab on its head is only playing dead: shoot it first or throw a grenade.
Tips: The buzz of flies often gives a zombie away. A shotgun is a good choice against every kind, and a zombie that loses its legs can keep coming.

sections.name: Fast Zombie
sections.card:
Summary: A skeletal zombie with 50 health that climbs, runs and leaps. Its leap hit does 10 and its double slash 6, and it often comes in packs of three to four.
Weak points: Its head: aim there with the shotgun or the .357. Hit it in mid-leap and it dies on the spot; the crossbow suits that best.
Looks like: No skin and few organs, so bone and muscle show, with long claws; it stands on two legs to slash but runs and climbs on all fours.
Tips: Alone it is weak, so the pack is the danger. It is much easier to hit at medium range, it cannot leap at you from behind cover, and it cannot attack you on a ladder, where it gets stuck below you.
Tips: Listen for its howl. On rooftops stay back from the edge: being startled off it costs fall damage. It climbs gutters that rattle as it comes, so shoot over the side before it reaches the top.

sections.name: Poison Zombie
sections.card:
Summary: A bloated, slow zombie with 175 health and a 20-damage slash. It carries three poison headcrabs on its back and throws them at you before it fights hand to hand.
Weak points: Fire: set it alight and the headcrabs on its back burn with it. Kill it before it throws and those headcrabs die too, so a crossbow bolt into the ones on its back ends it early.
Looks like: Bloated and reddish-purple, bent nearly double under the headcrabs on its back.
Tips: Carry fire to it: pick up a propane tank or gas canister with the gravity gun, light it up from cover, then duck back before it throws more. Grenades and explosive barrels cannot ignite it but still do decent damage.
Tips: A thrown poison headcrab drops you to 1 health, so keep moving up close and do not swing the crowbar at them while other enemies are around. Once all three are thrown it is little threat; the pulse rifle's energy ball disintegrates it.

sections.name: Antlion Guard
sections.card:
Summary: A huge antlion with 500 health. It charges from afar and butts you up close: a running head smash does 20, a headbutt 10, and it can also fling objects at you.
Weak points: It turns slowly, so strafing keeps you clear of its attacks, and a charge that ends in a wall stuns it for a few seconds. It is a big target for the shotgun, which is extremely effective against it.
Looks like: About 8.6 feet tall, with a hard dark-red shell, bright blue feather-like growths down its back, and a bulky, beak-tipped head it uses as a battering ram.
Tips: Its growls warn you before it attacks. Kill the soldier antlions that crowd you, but keep track of the guard. Swap between the crossbow, the RPG and the MP7's grenades so damage never pauses for a reload.
Tips: Launching explosive barrels or a car engine with the gravity gun saves ammo. The pulse rifle's secondary fire will not disintegrate it but hurts it badly. If it hurls something at you, dodge it or catch it and throw it back.

sections.name: Manhack
sections.card:
Summary: A small flying drone with 25 health and spinning blades. It crashes into its target with no care for itself, and is deadliest in vents, sewers and other tight places, usually in a group.
Weak points: The gravity gun is the best answer: pull one in and punt it into a wall, and it is destroyed at once.
Looks like: Three blades spinning so fast they whir, and a single camera eye that glows red while it is active.
Tips: A few pistol or SMG rounds kill it, but it bounces around when hit; a shotgun or magnum shot kills it at once. Three crowbar hits destroy it, though that puts you next to its blades.
Tips: Against several, use a fast-firing weapon like the SMG or pulse rifle, and deal with them quickly before they distract you from other threats. A manhack thrown through open air without hitting anything is only dazed.

sections.name: Barnacle
sections.card:
Summary: A ceiling-hanging mouth with a sticky tongue that hauls up anything that touches it. It has 35 health here and crushes for 10 again and again; it kills other characters outright with a neck snap, but not you.
Weak points: The crowbar kills it in one hit, and it dies if it swallows poison. A burning explosive barrel on its tongue kills it, and the barnacles hanging next to it too.
Looks like: Little more than a big mouth with two rows of sharp teeth, with a long string-like tongue dangling from a ceiling or overhang.
Tips: It takes a moment to tell food from junk and holds one thing at a time, so a tire, barrel or plank on its tongue lets you slip past.
Tips: Four or five pistol shots kill it, and if it grabs you, you can usually kill it before it swallows you. Do not crowbar a high one: you take fall damage as well as its attack.

sections.name: Combine Gunship
sections.card:
Summary: A big Combine flyer that only explosives hurt: 3, 5 or 7 RPG hits on easy, normal and hard. It shoots your rockets out of the air, and the Combine often send two together.
Weak points: Small arms do nothing; the RPG does. A rocket coming in at its rear or side meets a blind spot, and it cannot change target in the middle of a firing cycle, so fire while it is busy with someone else.
Looks like: A stubby round head and a wide body ending in a huge round rotor; green-brown camouflage with white splotches on top, white with teal underneath.
Tips: Never fly a rocket straight at it: steer around its head, zig-zag or corkscrew, or send it high and slam it down from above. A thud from its cannon warns that a burst is coming.
Tips: It fires ahead of you, and at explosive barrels near you, so stay clear of barrels or set them off first. To cross open ground to a rocket crate, fire a rocket into the air and steer it: the gunship goes after the rocket.
